title: Two Men Named Dan Sullivan Are on Alaska's Senate Ballot
summary:
President Donald Trump says he told the Justice Department to file a lawsuit about Alaska's Senate election. The lawsuit could block the result from being certified, but only if the Republican candidate who already holds the seat loses.

The problem is the ballot: it has two men named Dan Sullivan. The one who already holds the seat is Republican Senator Dan Sullivan, listed as Daniel S. The other is Dan J. Sullivan. Some Republicans worry voters may mix up the two names. Alaska's Supreme Court has already said Dan J. Sullivan can stay on the ballot.

The Justice Department says it filed the case to protect the election. President Trump says he ordered it, and he called Daniel J. the fake candidate. The report notes that Daniel J. Sullivan has voted in Alaska races before.

Election expert David Becker disagrees. He says this is only a state matter, so the Justice Department has no role in it. He also says trying to block certification 11 days before the vote has never happened before.
why_it_matters: Elections decide who speaks for your state, so understanding how ballots and courts work helps you see why fair voting rules matter.

After voting, officials check and certify the result, which means they confirm it is official.
In Alaska, two men with the same name are on the Senate ballot, and a court case argues about whether the result can be certified.
